text:
Toronto won in Vancouver on a night when the scoreboard flattered neither team much, and it came down to William Nylander. The winger, drafted 8th overall in 2014 out of MODO's junior program, opened the scoring 1:23 in on a backhand, set up Teddy Blueger's empty-looking insurance goal late in the third, and was named first star with a goal and an assist. Blueger's goal, at 18:24, came on an 85% chance and sealed a 4-2 TOR win.

The game was closer than 4-2 suggests. Our numbers give Toronto a slight edge in chance quality (expected goals, a measure of how dangerous each shot was): 3.97 to 2.77. By our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, Toronto came out at 56% and Vancouver at 44%. The Canucks had more shot attempts, 61 to 53, and the first period was theirs, 1.56 to 1.38 in expected goals. Marco Rossi had a 34% look stopped by Anthony Stolarz. Toronto took the second period, 1.55 to 0.26, and Auston Matthews and Zack MacEwen scored in it. MacEwen's slap shot was a 4% chance, the least likely goal of the game.

In goal, Stolarz stopped 26 of 28 and saved 0.77 more goals than expected from the shots he faced. Leevi Merilainen stopped 24 of 27, about what the chances called for. Vancouver got a power-play goal from Brock Boeser and a third-period goal from Max Sasson, but never drew level after the second period. Toronto left with the two points. Vancouver heads back to work after a loss that was more about two defining Toronto moments than a lopsided game.
